sessions.title: Migrating to Event Driven Architecture to Improve Communication Across 50+ Module
sessions.description: When our e-learning Flutter app grew to 50+ modules, the hardest part was not how to keep "each module independent," but rather how they "talked to each other." A codebase with 50+ modules and 25 engineers, split into 3 teams and simultaneously working on it, started to cause: - Conflict issues in code and dependencies. - Importing multiple other packages into a new feature module. - A refactor in the profile module broke all the other modules. - Code review challenges across multiple modules. This talk covers our migration to an event-driven architecture to solve the above problems and the learnings along the way.

sessions.description: TDD is not mainly about finding bugs later. The real idea is simpler: before you write any code, you write down what you expect it to do. AI coding assistants are good at generating code against a precise expectation and bad at inventing the right one from a vague prompt. sessions.title: Hardening Flutter Security: Balancing Compliance & Operational Risks

sessions.title: Flutter Can't Do That: Shipping AirPlay, HealthKit, and Live Activities
sessions.description: Sooner or later, every Flutter app hits a wall: a native framework with no `pub.dev` package, an abandoned plugin with dozens of unresolved issues, or a feature like a Live Activity in the Dynamic Island, that Flutter simply cannot render. At that point, you're writing platform code, and most of us do it the worst possible way: a hand-written `MethodChannel` with stringly-typed method names, custom codecs, and no compile-time safety across Dart, Swift, and Kotlin. This talk is about doing it properly with Pigeon, demonstrated through real integrations I built and documented not `getBatteryLevel()`.
